The key is defensible: expansionary fiscal policy and contractionary monetary policy both raise interest rates, while their effects on real GDP offset, so the net effect is indeterminate. Option B is the only choice that gives a determinate rise in interest rates with an indeterminate GDP effect. The other policy mixes give a determinate interest rate change (C) or a determinate GDP change (A, E), so no other option fits.

The "none" stimulus is acceptable for this standalone item. The AP exam commonly asks this kind of policy-mix question with the same five-option format.

The explanations for A, C and E are accurate. The item is short and non-computational, so the time and calculator load are fine.
